union.summary: Fix silently kills the single-dash setext heading (`Heading` + `-`) everywhere in the preview — broader than the reported bug
union.evidence:
`const isLoneDash = marker === DASH && runLength === 1;` disables setext-underline recognition for ANY lone `-`, not just an indented empty bullet nested under a list item. In CommonMark `Heading
-` is a perfectly valid `<h2>` (the same construct as `Heading
---`). The issue (#517) is scoped to "an indented, empty nested list item" under a parent `- 1`; nothing in it asks for top-level `Heading
-` to stop being a heading. The design-doc text added by this PR (docs/design/notes/notes.md:297-299) says "Multi-dash `---` and `=` setext underlines are untouched, so ordinary setext headings still render", which understates the loss: single-dash setext H2s no longer render, and the new tests only cover the `---` form (preview.test.ts 'preserves multi-dash setext headings'). Existing notes containing `Title
-` will re-render as a paragraph followed by an empty bullet list. This is unrequested behavior change / scope creep beyond the issue's outcome.

union.summary: Vendors a ~70-line verbatim fork of markdown-it's upstream `lheading` rule instead of wrapping/reusing it
union.evidence: `const lheadingRule: BlockRule = ...` is, by its own comment (line 67: "Mirrors the upstream rule (markdown-it 14.x `rules_block/lheading.mjs`) with a single added guard"), a copy of dependency-internal parser code with one extra `if`. packages/notes depends on `"markdown-it": "^14.1.0"` (packages/notes/package.json:63), a floating caret range, so any upstream fix to `lheading` (blockquote/lazy-continuation quirks, token map changes) silently stops applying to the notes preview. The repo's own precedent for extending the preview parser is the additive `md.block.ruler.before('paragraph', 'details', …)` in packages/notes/src/view/details-plugin.ts:104 — no upstream rule is forked there. The file already has `getRuleFn` (line 207) to delegate to the stock `list` rule, so the same delegate-and-guard shape was available for `lheading` too; duplicating the whole rule is reinvention of code that already exists in the dependency.

union.summary: Reaches into markdown-it's private `__rules__` registry to obtain the `list` rule function
union.evidence: `const ruler = md.block.ruler as unknown as { __rules__: … }` (with the comment "markdown-it's Ruler exposes no public getter, so we read its private `__rules__` registry"). This couples a first-party plugin to an undocumented internal of a caret-ranged dependency; if the field is renamed the plugin throws at module init (`markdown-it block rule not found`) and the whole notes preview dies, not just the empty-bullet case. The alternative supported layer — registering an additional rule with `ruler.before('list', …)` / `ruler.before('paragraph', …)`, as details-plugin.ts does — was not used or discussed in the task plan.

union.summary: Paragraph-interrupt relaxation also covers `*` and `+` empty bullets, wider than the issue or the documented "narrow" deviation
union.evidence: `isEmptyBulletLine` accepts `-`, `*` and `+` (`if (marker !== DASH && marker !== 0x2a && marker !== 0x2b) return false;`). Only `-` has the setext ambiguity described in issue #517; `*`/`+` empty bullets never produced an `<h2>` and were only refused as paragraph interrupters by CommonMark's empty-item rule. Allowing them widens the CommonMark deviation for cases nobody reported, and the design-doc wording added here calls the deviation "deliberate and narrow" around "a lone single `-`" (docs/design/notes/notes.md:293-296) without mentioning `*`/`+`. No test or acceptance criterion covers them either.

union.summary: Planned verification case "top-level lone dash" from the task plan was not delivered

The five tests added to packages/notes/src/view/preview.test.ts cover every item except the top-level lone dash — which is precisely the case where this change deviates most from CommonMark (`Heading\n-` no longer an `<h2>`). The delivered behavior for that input is therefore neither pinned nor acknowledged anywhere.

union.summary: Fix is broader than the issue: single-dash setext H2 (`Heading\n-`) is now impossible anywhere in the notes preview, not just inside a list
union.evidence: `const isLoneDash = marker === DASH && runLength === 1; if (pos >= max && !isLoneDash) { level = ... }` — the guard is unconditional on context: it applies at top level, at any indent, with or without a surrounding list. So a perfectly ordinary and valid CommonMark H2 written as `Title\n-` stops rendering as a heading and instead becomes a paragraph plus an empty bullet. The issue (#517) only asks that an *indented, empty nested bullet under a list item* not restyle its parent; nothing in it asks to drop single-dash setext headings. The plugin's own acceptance criteria only protect the multi-dash form (`Heading\n---`, see docs/tasks/active/20260724-notes-empty-bullet-setext-todo.md:70), so the single-dash regression is accepted silently rather than scoped out. A narrower condition (dash line indented relative to / inside an open list item, or `state.parentType`/blkIndent-aware) would satisfy the issue without regressing an unrelated documented Markdown construct.

union.summary: Vendored fork of markdown-it's upstream `lheading` rule (~70 lines copied) instead of wrapping/delegating like the `list` rule does in the same file
union.evidence: `const lheadingRule: BlockRule = (state, startLine, endLine) => { ... }` is, per its own comment, a copy of "upstream rule (markdown-it 14.x `rules_block/lheading.mjs`) with a single added guard", including a re-implementation of markdown-it's internal `asciiTrim` (line 17-22) and the token-pushing/`parentType` bookkeeping. The same file already demonstrates the non-duplicating pattern for `list` (`getRuleFn(md, 'list')` + `wrappedList` delegating to `originalList`), and a wrap-and-rollback or a pre-`lheading` guard rule would avoid holding a copy of third-party parser code. As written, any markdown-it upgrade silently diverges from the vendored copy with no test that can detect the drift. This is duplication of an existing (upstream) module rather than reuse, which this repo's reuse expectation disfavours.

union.summary: Unrequested scope: the paragraph-interrupt relaxation also covers `*` and `+` empty bullets, which are not implicated by the setext ambiguity
union.evidence: `if (marker !== DASH && marker !== 0x2a /* * */ && marker !== 0x2b /* + */) return false;` in `isEmptyBulletLine`. Only `-` can be a setext underline, so only `-` is needed for issue #517. Allowing empty `*`/`+` bullets to interrupt a paragraph changes rendering for inputs the issue never mentions (e.g. `foo\n*` becomes paragraph + empty list instead of a single paragraph), a CommonMark deviation with no acceptance criterion and no test behind it.

union.summary: Approach relies on markdown-it's private `__rules__` registry when a public-API path exists
union.evidence: `const ruler = md.block.ruler as unknown as { __rules__: Array<{ name: string; fn: BlockRule; enabled: boolean }> };` plus the manual `alt: ['paragraph','reference','blockquote']` restoration hazard documented at line 196-200. The same effect is reachable through the public `md.block.ruler.before('list', '<name>', fn, { alt: ['paragraph'] })`: a new rule that returns true in silent mode for an empty bullet and false otherwise, letting the stock `list` rule run untouched. Reaching into an undocumented internal is a wrong-layer choice that couples the notes preview to markdown-it's internal shape.
